DAMGHANI:v1p34/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p34/r2.claim: Al-akl can mean eating itself; Ṭā Hā is a parallel.
DAMGHANI:v1p34/r2.anchor: الأكل بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r1.claim: The command begins with an understood and We said; its explanation had already appeared in al-Baqara, where the food is called abundant, a phrase omitted here for brevity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r1.anchor: أي وقلنا يا آدم وتقدم تفسير هذه الآية في البقرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r2.claim: The wording in al-Baqara is fuller because that sūra is Medinan, whereas this Meccan passage expresses the same meaning more briefly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p24/r2.anchor: وحذف رغدا هنا على سبيل الاختصار وأثبت هناك لأن تلك مدنية وهذه مكية

ASAD-NOTES:7:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:intro/r3.claim: Human weakness and susceptibility to appetite, vanity, and false self-interest make continuing prophetic guidance necessary; Adam and Eve's fall and Iblis's temptation illustrate this condition.
ASAD-NOTES:7:intro/r3.anchor: The need for continued prophetic guidance arises from the fact of man's weakness

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.claim: Verses 11–27 recount Adam's creation, temptation, and expulsion from the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.anchor:
the story of Adam’s creation, temptation, and exile from
the Garden.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r12.claim: Humanity's original station in creation is high and delicate: the angels prostrated while Iblis did not, before Adam and his spouse were told to dwell in the garden.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r12.anchor: İnsanın asl-ı hilkatindeki mevki‘i böyle yüksek ve nâziktir.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r13.speaker: bazı kaviller
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r13.claim: One reported view identifies the garden where Adam and his spouse dwelt as the Garden of Eternity.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r13.anchor: cennetü’l-huld[^29] veya semâ cennetlerinden bir cennet

ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r14.speaker: bazı kaviller
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r14.claim: Another reported view identifies Adam's garden as one of the gardens in heaven.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r14.anchor: veya semâ cennetlerinden bir cennet veya Arz cennetlerinden bir cennet

ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r15.speaker: bazı kaviller
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r15.claim: A further reported view identifies Adam's garden as an earthly garden.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r15.anchor: semâ cennetlerinden bir cennet veya Arz cennetlerinden bir cennet olması hakkında bazı kaviller vardır

ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r16.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says the garden from which Iblis was expelled and in which Adam lived was the Garden of Eden, not the Garden of Eternity.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r16.anchor: İbn Abbas radıyallâhu anhümâ “cennetü’lhuldde değil cennet-i adnde idiler” demiştir.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r17.claim: With dāl unvowelled, adn means residence and shares a root with maʿdin; the name evokes the garden as the original place of creation and residence, where Adam first received the blessing of existence.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r17.anchor: Dâlin sükûnuyla “Adn” ikāmet demek olduğuna ve “ma‘din” kelimesinin de esası bulunduğuna nazaran

ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r18.claim: Since the named gardens of Eden are among the gardens of the afterlife, Elmalılı suggests Adam's first garden was the first garden on the way to the Garden of Eternity, where beginning and return meet, as 43:72 indicates.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#4/r18.anchor: mebde’ ile me‘âdın bir telâkīsi bulunacağı anlaşılabilir.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.claim: Adam and Eve could eat from anything in Paradise, with the single forbidden tree serving as their trial.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p17/.anchor: They were just stopped from going near one tree and it was this tree that became a trial for them.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r46.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r46.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r46.claim: The account parallels 2:35. Adam’s wife is Eve, called Ḥawwāʾ in Islamic tradition, though the Quran never names her.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r46.anchor: Eve, or Ḥawwāʾ in Arabic, whose name does not appear in the Quran, although it is commonly used in the Islamic tradition.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.claim: Eve enters without an account of her origin; although primordial Adam represents all humanity, male and female, the Quran does not explain how this Adam becomes the first couple.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.anchor: the Quran does not explicitly discuss the process by which this primordial Adam is differentiated into the first male and female

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r48.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r48.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r48.claim: The Bible’s rib account appears in Hadith; many commentators read 4:1 as an oblique reference to Eve’s creation from Adam, understood here as primordial and androgynic humanity.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r48.anchor: The Biblical story of Eve’s creation from Adam’s rib (Genesis 2:21–22), however, is referenced in the Ḥadīth

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r49.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r49.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r49.claim: Adam and Eve may eat any Garden fruit except the forbidden tree, variously identified as wheat, fig, or grape and called the Tree of Everlastingness elsewhere; this differs from the Biblical tree of knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r49.anchor: commentators variously describe as a wheat or grain plant, a fig tree, or a grapevine

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r71.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r71.speaker: Qu
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r71.claim: The statement that God called out to Adam and Eve signals distance and alienation, unlike His intimate direct address to Adam earlier.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r71.anchor: it is said that He called out to them, an expression that indicates distance and alienation

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r2.claim: Some interpreters call the prostration command and tree prohibition ontological, but Tabataba’i rejects this: such commands cannot be disobeyed, while both Iblis and Adam disobeyed.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r2.anchor: الأمر والنهي التكوينيين لا يقبلان التخلف والمخالفة، وقد خالف إبليس الأمر وخالف آدم النهي

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r3.claim: As explained earlier in the discussion of al-Baqara, God placed Adam in a heavenly intermediate garden before earthly life and legal responsibility to test human nature.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r3.anchor: خلق جنة برزخية سماوية، وأدخل آدم فيها قبل أن يستقر عليه الحياة الأرضية

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r4.claim: The garden was neither the eternal paradise from which no one exits nor an ordinary worldly home governed by legislative commands.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r4.anchor: ولا الدار كانت دارا دنيوية يعاش فيها عيشة دنيوية يديرها التشريع ويحكم فيها الأمر والنهي المولويان

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r5.claim: The garden manifests human disposition generally, not Adam’s disposition as an individual; humanity must mature on earth under commands and prohibitions and attain happiness through obedience.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r5.anchor: بل كانت دارا يظهر فيها حكم السجية الإنسانية لا سجية آدم عليه السلام بما هو شخص آدم

TAB-FULL:v10p106/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p106/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p106/r1.claim: After expelling Iblis from the Garden, God settled Adam and his wife there, allowed them to eat fruit wherever they wished, and forbade them to approach one particular tree.
TAB-FULL:v10p106/r1.anchor: وأباح لهما أن يأكلا من ثمارها من أي مكان شاءا منها، ونهاهما أن يقربا ثمر شجرة بعينها

TAB-FULL:v10p106/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p106/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p106/r2.claim: Being among the wrongdoers means opposing the Lord’s command and doing what one has no right to do; Tabari gives the same gloss at 2:35.
TAB-FULL:v10p106/r2.anchor: يقول: فتكونا ممن خالف أمر ربه، وفعل ما ليس له فعله

TABATABAI:7:18-20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r5.claim: Adam alone is directly addressed, while his wife is included in the ruling.
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r5.anchor: خص بالخطاب آدم عليه السلام وألحق به في الحكم زوجته

TABATABAI:7:18-20/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r6.claim: The permission to eat wherever they wished broadly allows their use of the Garden, except for the tree singled out next.
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r6.anchor: توسعة في إباحة التصرف إلا ما استثناه

TABATABAI:7:18-20/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r7.claim: Their “wronging” themselves means self-harm, not disobedience to a binding legislative command, since the prohibition was guidance.
TABATABAI:7:18-20/r7.anchor: والظلم هو الظلم على النفس دون معصية الأمر المولوي فإن الأمر إرشادي

TABATABAI:7:20-25/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī refers readers to his fuller discussion of the Garden story in the commentary on al-Baqara.
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r10.anchor: وقد مر تفصيل الكلام في قصة الجنة في سورة البقرة فليراجعها من شاء

TABRISI:7:18-20/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r8.claim: The command is to dwell in the Garden, not merely to be still; zawjatuka is omitted because the possessive phrase already conveys its meaning concisely.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r8.anchor: هذا أمر بالسكنى دون السكون وإنما لم يقل وزوجتك لأن الإضافة إليه قد أغنت عن ذكره

TABRISI:7:18-20/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r9.claim: God permits the two to eat from wherever they wish, in whatever place or manner they choose.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r9.anchor: أباح سبحانه لهما أن يأكلا من حيث شاءا وأين شاءا أو ما شاءا

TABRISI:7:18-20/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r10.claim: The prohibition against approaching the tree means they must not eat from it.

TABRISI:7:18-20/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:18-20/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:18-20/r11.claim: They would wrong themselves by forfeiting the great reward.
TABRISI:7:18-20/r11.anchor: أي من الباخسين نفوسهم الثواب العظيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p60/r1.claim: The explanation of this verse is given in Surat al-Baqara.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r1.claim: The author says the explanation of Adam being told to dwell in the Garden was already given in al-Baqara.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:19-22/r1.anchor: { ويا آدم اسكن } سبق تفسيره في سورة البقرة.

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r1.claim: Adam and Eve may eat where they wish, but their permission is bounded; the forbidden tree marks a limit rather than granting unlimited freedom or ownership.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r1.anchor: bu salâhiyet ve me’zûniyet her kayıttan âzâde gayr-i mahdûd bir hürriyet ve temlik olmayıp

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r2.claim: A tree marks a spatial boundary and eating its fruit a limit on action; although within paradise, its vicinity became a testing ground for Adam and Eve.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r2.anchor: Haddinizi tecavüz ve kendinize yazık etmiş bulunursunuz

ELMALILI:7:19-22/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r3.claim: Adam remained subject to obligation even in paradise; transgressing the limits and rights God set makes anyone unjust to himself.
ELMALILI:7:19-22/r3.anchor: Âdem’in cennette bile mebde’-i mükellefiyetten âzâde olmadığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:19/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:19/r1.speaker: Bir görüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:19/r1.claim: One view takes this garden in its lexical sense as an earthly, garden-like place where Adam and Eve were to live.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:19/r1.anchor: Bir görüşe göre bu cennet, sözlük anlamıyla “dünyadaki bağlık bahçelik bir yer” olup Âdem ve Havvâ’nın burada yaşamaları istenmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:19/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:19/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:19/r2.claim: Considering the related verses together, the author concludes that Adam was created on earth from special soil, his mate from him, and both were then placed in the eternal reward Paradise, whose life differs from earthly life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:19/r2.anchor: İlk insanı Allah özel bir topraktan yeryüzünde yaratmış, ondan eşini de var etmiş, sonra bunları cennete koymuştur. Bu cennetin ve içindeki hayatın yeryüzündeki hayattan farklı

QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r10.claim: God placed the means of trial with Adam in the Garden: his spouse and the tree of ordeal; the tree’s presence reflects the hidden mystery of divine allotment.
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r10.anchor: وأي نقص يكون في الجنة لو لم يخلق فيها تلك الشجرة التي هي شجرة المحنة

BURHAN:v4p144/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p144/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p144/r2.claim: In “do not approach this tree lest you become wrongdoers,” the verb after ف may be jussive, extending the prohibition to becoming wrongdoers, or subjunctive, expressing the consequence.
BURHAN:v4p144/r2.anchor: يحتمل إن يكون ما بعد الفاء مجزوما ويحتمل إن يكون منصوبا

BURHAN:v2p410/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p410/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p410/r7.claim: A connected subject pronoun is conventionally reinforced by an independent pronoun when coordinated with a noun.
BURHAN:v2p410/r7.anchor: الثامن تأكيد الضمير ويجب ان يؤكد المتصل بالمنفصل اذا عطف عليه

BURHAN:v4p145/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p145/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p145/r9.claim: The prohibition against approaching the tree, followed by its consequence, is cited as a parallel.
BURHAN:v4p145/r9.anchor: ﴿ ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين ﴾

SULAMI:v1p223#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p223#3/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p223#3/r1.claim: One account says Adam understood the prohibition to concern the particular tree indicated, while God intended its whole kind; he took another, and repented for failing to be cautious rather than for disobedience.

SULAMI:v1p223#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p223#3/r2.speaker: الخراز
SULAMI:v1p223#3/r2.claim: Al-Kharr az says the command and prohibition made Adam uneasy even in Paradise; God let the lapse occur so its lesson and proof would emerge, then expelled and reproached him, with 20:115 also cited.
SULAMI:v1p223#3/r2.anchor: قال الخراز : والله ما هنىء آدم الجنة ولا سكناها

ITQAN:v3p304/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p304/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p304/r4.claim: Baqara’s ‘and eat’ uses waw to join dwelling and eating, while al-A‘raf’s fa follows taking a dwelling; ‘freely’ and ‘wherever you wish’ there fit the broader wording.
ITQAN:v3p304/r4.anchor: قيل لأن السكنى في البقرة الإقامة وفي الأعراف اتخاذ المسكن

ITQAN:v3p305/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p305/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p305/r1.claim: In comparing Adam’s garden instructions, al-Araf’s fa marks eating as following the commanded taking up of residence, while min ḥaythu is less general than ḥaythu shiʾtum.
ITQAN:v3p305/r1.anchor: وفي الأعراف ﴿ ويا آدم ﴾ فأتى بالفاء الدالة على ترتيب الأكل على السكنى المأمور باتخاذها

DAMGHANI:v1p420/r26.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r26.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r26.claim: Lā can mark prohibition, as in the ban on approaching the tree or consuming one another's property unjustly.
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r26.anchor: لا بمعنى النهي قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

NAHHAS:v2p117/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p117/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p117/r9.claim: The command is a prohibition, and ‘then you will be among the wrongdoers’ is its coordinated consequence.
NAHHAS:v2p117/r9.anchor: 19 نهى ( فتكونا من الظالمين ) جواب ويكون عطف

SAMIN-DURR:7:19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:19/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:19/r1.claim: The word رغدا found in al-Baqara is omitted here, but context indicates it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:19/r1.anchor: وفي البقرة: { رغدا }: وهو محذوف لدلالة الكلام عليه

ZAJJAJ:v2p325/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p325/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p325/r3.claim: Including the independent pronoun أنت is the better construction; اذهب وزيد without it would be awkward.
ZAJJAJ:v2p325/r3.anchor: هذا الاختيار، أعني ذكر أنت، تقول اذهب أنت وزيد، ولو قلت: اذهب وزيد كان قبيحا.

ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r1.claim: Some identify the forbidden tree as wheat; another view identifies it as a grapevine.
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم: هي السنبلة، وقيل هي شجرة الكرم.

ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r2.claim: The preferred parse makes فتكونا accusative as the consequence of the prohibition: if they approach, they become wrongdoers.
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r2.anchor: " فتكونا " في موضع نصب على جوانب الأمر بالفاء.

ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r3.claim: Alternatively فتكونا is jussive, coordinated with the prohibition: do not approach, and so do not become wrongdoers.
ZAJJAJ:v2p326/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع جزم عطفا على قوله: ولا تقربا فتكونا

ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n13/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to the parallel accounts and notes at 2:35 and 20:120.
ASAD-NOTES:7:19#n13/r1.anchor: See 2:35 and 20:120, as well as the corresponding notes.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r5.claim: The mention of 'abundantly' in al-Baqara suits its enumeration of blessings and honor, whereas both al-Aʿrāf stories omit it amid punishment and reproach; this parallels Moses and Adam.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r5.anchor: لأنه مناسب لتعداد النعم ولم يقل: (رغداً) في سورة الأعراف لأن المقام تقريع وتأنيب

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r3.claim: Al-Baqara attributes the command directly to God with “We said,” an expression of favor and honor; al-Aʿraf joins Adam’s dwelling command to Iblis’s expulsion under one “He said.”
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r3.anchor: فقد أسند القولَ في البقرة إلى نفسه (وقلنا يا آدم) وهذا يقوله القرآن في مقام التكريم والتعظيم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r4.claim: Al-Baqara adds “freely” because its scene gives Adam greater honor, unlike the al-Aʿraf setting.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r4.anchor: وناسب التكريم والتعظيم أن يذكر (رغداً) في البقرة دون الأعراف لأن المقامين مختلفان.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r5.speaker: الكرماني
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r5.claim: Al-Kirmānī says al-Baqara adds “freely” because its report is elevated by the added divine attribution “We said,” unlike al-Aʿraf.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r5.anchor: جاء في (البرهان) للكرماني: "وزاد في البقرة (رغداً) لما زاد في الخبر تعظيماً بقوله: (وقلنا)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r6.speaker: التفسير الكبير
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r6.claim: The Tafsīr al-Kabīr explains that wāw denotes unrestricted coordination and fa denotes sequence, with sequence a narrower case within the broader meaning.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r6.anchor: جاء في (التفسير الكبير) : "قال في سورة البقرة: (وكلا منها رغداً) بالواو

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r7.claim: The wāw leaves timing open and signals wider choice, whereas fa requires eating immediately after settling; the broader permission fits al-Baqara’s honorific setting.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r7.anchor: فالواو صالحة لجميع الأزمان بما فيها معنى الفاء. أما الفاء فتفيد التعقيب، أي:

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r8.claim: Al-Baqara repeats the garden reference in “from it,” fitting its more honorific presentation; al-Aʿraf omits that pronoun.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r8.anchor: فقد أعاد ضمير الجنة في البقرة مع الأكل فقال: (منها) ولم يُعِدْهُ في الأعراف.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r9.claim: In al-Baqara “wherever you wish” can govern both dwelling and eating, but in al-Aʿraf it can only govern eating, making the former permission wider.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r9.anchor: فالمشيئة والتخيير في البقرة أوسع لأنها تشمل السكن والأكل بخلاف الأعراف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r10.claim: A slip can occur without moving downward, while “lowering” implies descent; the two expressions therefore differ in severity and direction.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r10.anchor: والإزلال غير التَدْلِيَةِ فإن الزلة قد تكون في الموضع نفسه، وأما التدلية فلا تكون إلا إلى أسفل،

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r11.claim: Al-Baqara calls the offense a slip to soften it in the honorific context; al-Aʿraf uses the harsher “lowered them through deception.”
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r11.anchor: فخفف المعصية في البقرة وسماها زلة مراعاة لمقام التكريم بخلاف الأعراف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r12.claim: Al-Baqara omits God’s reproach of Adam and his wife, while al-Aʿraf includes it; reproach is a lower degree of honor than no reproach.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r12.anchor: ولا شك أن مرتبة العتاب أدنى من عدمه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r13.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r13.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r13.claim: The reproach of humanity’s parents in al-Aʿraf matches the preceding rebuke of their descendants for being little grateful.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r13.anchor: ثم انظر كيف ناسب هذا العتاب لأبوي البشر في الجنة عتاب أبنائهما في الدنيا

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r14.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r14.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r14.claim: Al-Baqara spares Adam explicit confession of sin, whereas al-Aʿraf reports his confession, consistent with their honor and reproach settings.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r14.anchor: طوى في البقرة تصريح آدم عن نفسه بالمعصية ولم يذكرها إكراماً له في حين ذكرها في الأعراف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r15.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r15.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r15.claim: Adam’s regret in al-Aʿraf echoes the confession of the communities punished just before the story.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r15.anchor: وانظر بعد هذا كيف يتسق ندم آدم ههنا مع ما ذكره قبل القصة من ندم المعاقبين من بني آدم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r16.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r16.claim: Adam’s verbal “we wronged” marks a passing slip, while his descendants’ nominal “we were wrongdoers” signals settled persistence; God forgives the former and destroys the latter.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r16.anchor: فقد قال آدم: (ظلمنا) بالصيغة الفعلية الدالة على الحدوث والطروء للدلالة على أنها زلَّةٌ طارئة وليست معصية إصرار.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r17.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r17.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r17.claim: Al-Baqara says Adam received words and God accepted his repentance without reporting a plea; al-Aʿraf reports his plea for forgiveness and mercy without mentioning acceptance, fitting each context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r17.anchor: ذكر في البقرة أن آدم تلقى من ربه كلمات فتاب عليه ولم يذكر ذلك في الأعراف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r18.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r18.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r18.claim: Al-Baqara promises that those who follow guidance will have no fear or grief, a mark of honor and a promise of return to Paradise.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r18.anchor: والتكريم واضح في هذه الآية إذ فيها وعد لمن تبع الهدى بالعودة إلى الجنة حيث لا خوف ولا حزن

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r19.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r19.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r19.claim: Al-Baqara uses the lighter form “follow”; Ṭā Hā uses the intensive form, suiting its more demanding guidance and easing the burden in al-Baqara’s honorific context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r19.anchor: ذلك أن الفعل المشدد يفيد المبالغة فاكتفى في البقرة بالأخف من الحدث ولم يشدد عليهم تخفيفاً على البشر

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r20.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r20.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r20.claim: The light verb “follow” recurs more in al-Baqara than in any other sūra, making it especially fitting there.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r20.anchor: فوضعه في مكانه الذي هو أليق به

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r21.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r21.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r21.claim: The lighter form accompanies God’s direct first-person attribution in al-Baqara, while the intensified form accompanies third-person “He said” in Ṭā Hā, matching the respective tones.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r21.anchor: أن التخفيف الذي يفيد التلطف بالعباد جاء مع إسناد القول إلى نفسه وأن التشديد جاء مع إسناد القول إلى الغائب

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r22.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r22.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r22.claim: Al-Baqara’s “no fear or grief” concerns the afterlife; Ṭā Hā’s “neither stray nor suffer” spans worldly life and the afterlife, with suffering tied to Adam’s expulsion.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r22.anchor: ومنها: أن نهاية الآية في البقرة تتعلق بالآخرة وهو قوله تعالى: {وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ} أي: في الآخرة. ونهاية الآية في (طه) تتعلق بالدنيا والآخرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r23.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r23.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r23.claim: Because Ṭā Hā covers both worldly striving against error and afterlife success, it uses the intensified form for the greater effort; al-Baqara concerns afterlife success alone.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#2/r23.anchor: والحالة الأولى تتطلب عملاً أكثر وأشق فجاء الفعل الدال على المبالغة والتكلف للأمر الشاق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p802/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p802/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p802/r1.claim: Baqara adds rag̱adan, a detail Samarrai considers fitting to that sūra’s honoring tone; al-Aʿrāf omits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p802/r1.anchor: المناسب للتكريم في السورة بينما لم ترد في سورة الأعراف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p802/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p802/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p802/r2.claim: Baqara’s wāw joins dwelling and eating without fixing sequence, allowing unbounded choice; al-Aʿrāf’s fa orders eating immediately after dwelling. Wāw can indicate order but is not limited to it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p802/r2.anchor: لا مانع أن تأتي الواو للترتيب لكن لا تُحصر للترتيب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p803/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p803/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p803/r1.claim: In Baqara, ḥaythu shiʾtumā can govern both dwelling and eating, widening Adam’s choices; in al-Aʿrāf, min ḥaythu shiʾtumā concerns only where they eat, matching the narrower fa.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p803/r1.anchor: في سورة البقرة تحتمل أن تكون للسكن والأكل؛ بمعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p803/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p803/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p803/r2.claim: Baqara’s azallahumā can mean a slip without descent and softens the lapse in an honoring context; al-Aʿrāf’s dallāhumā explicitly lowers them, fitting its punitive context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p803/r2.anchor: والتدلية لا تكون إلا من أعلى لأسفل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r1.claim: The implied “We said” is understood from 2:35; many investigators connect this whole episode to the earlier command to the angels, as a continuation of favor to humanity and honor for Adam.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r1.anchor: أي وقلنا كما وقع في سورة البقرة فهذه القصة بتمامها معطوفة على مثلها وهو قوله سبحانه : ( قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r2.claim: Some argue the sequence calls for connecting Adam’s command to the preceding “Iblīs, leave”; al-Ālūsī says this has an argument but conflicts with the apparent reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r2.anchor: وادعى بعضهم أن الذي يقتضيه الترتيب العطف على ما بعد ( قال )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r3.claim: Beginning with a direct call signals the importance of the command; addressing Adam alone marks his precedence in receiving and carrying it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r3.anchor: وتصدير الكلام بالنداء للتنبيه على الاهتمام بالمأمور به

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r4.claim: “Dwell” means residence, staying, and settling, not stillness as the opposite of movement.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r4.anchor: و ( اسكن ) من السكنى وهو الليث والاقامة والاستقرار دون السكون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r5.claim: Addressing both Adam and Eve in the permission to eat honors them equally and shows they share the act; Eve follows Adam regarding residence, while the prohibition explicitly addresses both.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r5.anchor: لتعميم التشريف والإيذان بتساويهما في مباشرة المأمور به فإن حواء أسوة له عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r6.claim: The meaning is “eat from it wherever you wish,” as in 2:35; “freely/abundantly” is omitted here because it was stated there.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r6.anchor: والمعنى فكلا منها حيث شئتما كما في البقرة ولم يذكر ( رغدا ) هنا ثقة بما ذكر هناك

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r7.claim: The prohibition on approaching the tree emphatically forbids eating from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r7.anchor: مبالغة في النهي عن الأكل منها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r8.claim: The reading hādhī is the original form: the yāʾ was deleted and replaced by hāʾ of compensation, not a pause marker.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r8.anchor: وهو الأصل إلا أنه حذفت الياء وعوض عنها الهاء فهي هاء عوض لا هاء سكت

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r9.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jinnī argues that the original was dhī from the masculine dhā and the diminutive dhayyā; the yāʾ was reduced and the remaining one changed to alif to avoid an awkward ending.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن جني : ويدل على أن الأصل هو الياء قولهم في المذكر : ذا والألف بدل من الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r10.claim: “You become” can be jussive, coordinated with “approach,” or subjunctive as the consequence of the prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p98#2/r10.anchor: يحتمل الجزم على العطف على ( تقربا ) والنصب على أنه جواب النهي

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r6.claim: The implied wording is “And We said: O Adam.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r6.anchor: أي وقلنا يا آدم. { اسكن أنت

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r7.claim: The variant hādhī is described as original from the diminutive dhayyā, with hāʾ substituted for yāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r7.anchor: هذي وهو الأصل لتصغيره على ذيا والهاء بدل

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r8.claim: The warning means they would become people who wronged themselves.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r9.claim: Takūnā may be jussive by coordination or subjunctive as the consequence of the prohibition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:18-19/r9.anchor: وتكونا يحتمل الجزم على العطف والنصب على الجواب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r8.claim: The explicit أنت confirms that the command addresses Adam himself, not a metonymic substitute among those associated with him.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r8.anchor: ولما كان المراد بهذا الأمر هو نفسه لا التجوز به بعض من يلابسه أكد ضميره لتصحيح العطف ورفع التجوز

BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r9.claim: The fāʾ in 'then eat' indicates that eating accompanied settlement in the Garden; al-Baqara's conjunction with waw does not conflict, since a specific sequence is contained within a general one.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r9.anchor: العطف بالفاء الدال على أن المأكول كان مع الإسكان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r10.claim: The phrase means ample provision and permits eating from everything in the Garden except the forbidden tree; al-Baqara additionally indicates freedom to eat anywhere there.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r10.anchor: من حيث شئتما } بمعنى رغدا أي واسعا فإنه يدل على إباحة الأكل من كل شيء فيها غير المنهي عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r11.claim: Prohibiting even approach is stronger than merely forbidding eating: one who comes near a forbidden boundary may fall into the act itself.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r11.anchor: أكد تحريمها بالنهي عن قربانها دون الاكتفاء بالنهي عن غشيانها فقال : { ولا تقربا } اي فضلا عن أن تتناولا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r12.claim: Eating after approaching the tree would make them wrongdoers, like people walking in darkness; the episode warns that disobeying God can destroy even the highest station.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p14/r12.anchor: أي بالأكل منها الذي هو مقصود النهي فتكونا بذلك فاعلين فعل من يمشي في الظلام

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya reports that God created Adam on Friday and placed him in the Garden of Firdaws that same day.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس ، عن ابى العالية قال : قال الله تبارك وتعالى : ويا ادم اسكن انت وزوجك الجنة قال : خلق الله ادم يوم الجمعة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r2.claim: Al-Suddī recounts that Adam first lived alone in the Garden, then awoke to a woman made from his rib to be his companion; she was named Ḥawwāʾ because she came from something living.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r2.anchor: عن السدي قال : اخرج ابليس من الجنة واسكن ادم الجنة فكان يمشي فيها وحشا ليس له زوج يسكن اليها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r3.speaker: أشعث الحداني
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r3.claim: Ashʿath al-Ḥaddānī says Ḥawwāʾ was one of the women of the Garden, and her pregnancy was so clear that the child’s sex could be seen.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r3.anchor: سمعت اشعث الحداني يقول : كانت حواء من نساء الجنة ، وكان الولد يرى في بطنها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r4.claim: Mujāhid says Adam and his wife could eat wherever they wished without being held to account.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد - يعني قوله : فكلا من حيث شئتما - قال : لاحساب عليكم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the forbidden tree as a grapevine; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Shaʿbī, Jaʿd ibn Hubayra, al-Suddī, and Muḥammad ibn Qays agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1448/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قال : الشجرة التي نهى عنها ادم الكرم . وروى عن سعيد بن جبير

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r1.claim: Qatāda says God tested Adam as He had tested the angels before; all creation is tested for obedience, and Adam's trial continued until he violated the prohibition.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا من الظالمين . قال : ابتلى الله ادم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r2.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says the tree was barley; each grain in the Garden was as large as a cow's liver, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r2.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه انه كان يقول : هي البر ولكن الحبة منها في الجنة ككلى البقر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r3.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r3.claim: Abū Mālik identifies the forbidden tree as a date palm.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r3.anchor: عن حصين عن ابى مالك : ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة قال : النخلة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r4.claim: Qatāda identifies the forbidden tree as a fig; Mujāhid and Ibn Jurayj report the same view.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r4.anchor: عن قتادة : ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة قال : هي التين . وروى عن مجاهد

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says eating from the tree caused bodily evacuation, which would be improper in the Garden.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r5.anchor: عن الربيع عن ابى العالية قال : كانت الشجرة من اكل منها احدث ، ولا ينبغي ان يكون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r6.claim: Wahb says the tree had intertwined, branching limbs and bore fruit eaten by angels for immortality; this was the fruit forbidden to Adam and his wife.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1449/r6.anchor: سمعت وهب بن منبه يقول : لما اسكن الله تعالى ادم وزوجه الجنة ، نهاه عن الشجرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r1.claim: The wāw before Adam’s address coordinates it within the quoted speech that began with the order to expel Iblis, rather than with the narrator’s preceding speech verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r1.anchor: الواو من قوله : { ويا آدم } عاطفة على جملة : { أخرج منها مذءوما مدحورا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r2.claim: A speaker may turn from one addressee to another in the same setting without repeating ‘We said’; this arrangement heightens the humiliation of expelled Iblis as Adam receives favor before him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r2.anchor: وفي توجيه الخطاب لآدم بهذه الفضيلة بحضور إبليس بعد طرده زيادة إهانة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r3.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r3.claim: He cites the Prophet’s judgment in the case of a man and an Ansari: the sheep and servant woman were returned, the son received one hundred lashes and a year’s exile, and Unays was sent to investigate the wife’s confession.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r3.anchor: قول النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم في قضية الرجل والأنصاري الذي كان ابن الرجل عسيفا عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r4.claim: If Adam was already created in Paradise, ‘dwell’ means remain there; if he was created elsewhere, it grants him entry as an honor. Either reading taunts Iblis, who had scorned Adam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r4.anchor: فالأمر في قوله : { اسكن } إنما هو أمر تقرير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r5.claim: The scene’s placement gives the wording an additional meaning beyond its parallel in al-Baqara: it shows Adam honored in the setting where Iblis is being punished and expelled.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r5.anchor: فقد دل موقع هذا الكلام ، في هذه السورة ، على معنى عظيم من قمع إبليس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r6.claim: The arrangement exemplifies a speaker addressing multiple people in one gathering, as in the ruler’s separate instructions to Joseph and his wife in 12:28–29.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p52#2/r6.anchor: ومن أسلوب هذه الآية ما في قوله تعالى : { قال إنه من كيدكن إن كيدكن عظيم يوسف أعرض عن هذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r1.claim: The A‘raf address is directed to polytheists who made Satan their patron, while the parallel in al-Baqara admonishes Israelites who are wary of Satan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r1.anchor: إن هذا الكلام مسوق إلى المشركين الذين اتخذوا الشيطان وليا من دون الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r2.claim: The vocative calls attention to Adam and honors him before the gathered company.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r2.anchor: والنداء للإقبال على آدم والتنويه بذكره في ذلك الملا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r3.claim: The explicit detached pronoun after the imperative further humiliates Iblis by implying that Adam is unlike him; context allows this indirect contrast even though pronouns have no inherent contrastive force.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r3.anchor: والإتيان بالضمير المنفصل بعد الأمر ، لقصد زيادة التنكيل بإبليس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r4.claim: The fa here, unlike the wāw in 2:35, makes permission to eat follow immediately on the order to dwell, signaling prompt and complete favor that intensifies Iblis’s distress.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r4.anchor: فالآية هنا أفادت أن الله تعالى أذن آدم بأن يتمتع بثمار الجنة عقب أمره بسكنى الجنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r5.claim: In al-Baqara the focus is reminding Israelites of Adam’s favor, sin, and repentance and warning them against Satan’s guile, so the audience and narrative purpose differ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r5.anchor: وأما آية البقرة فإنما أفادت السامعين أن الله امتن على آدم بمنة سكنى الجنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r6.claim: He adds that the subtle implication of the detached pronoun in this address also applies to al-Baqara, though he had previously missed it there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p53#2/r6.anchor: وهذه نكتة فاتني العلم بها في آية سورة البقرة فضمها إليها أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r1.claim: The al-Baqara account also honors Adam with the word ‘abundantly’ (raghadan); together the two accounts distribute several favors across the story.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r1.anchor: على أن آية البقرة ( 35 ) لم تخل عن ذكر ما فيه تكرمة له وهو قوله : رغدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r2.claim: Banning even approach to the tree warns more strongly than banning its fruit, by blocking the means that could lead to eating it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r2.anchor: وقوله : { ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة } أشد في التحذير من أن ينهى عن الأكل منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r3.claim: The prohibition was probably a test: one tree was excluded amid permitted trees to train resistance to appetite and gradually establish humanity’s cognitive faculties through its first ancestor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r3.anchor: وهذا هو الظاهر ليتكون مختلف القوى العقلية في عقل النوع بتأسيسها في أصل النوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r4.claim: On this account, Adam’s first impulse to disobey and eating from the tree brought an instinctive awareness of shortcomings and ended his simple, naive state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r4.anchor: فأعقبه الأكل حدوث خاطر الشعور بما فيه من نقايص أدركها بالفطرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r5.claim: An alternative says the tree’s nature awakened knowledge of good and evil, as in the Torah’s account of the tree of knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ذلك لخصوصية في طبع تلك الشجرة أن تثير في النفس علم الخير والشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur regards the intrinsic knowledge-tree explanation as unlikely; he reads the story as depicting human cognition’s development, like Adam’s learning the names in 2:31.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r6.anchor: وهذا عندي بعيد ، وإنما حكى الله لنا هيئة تطور العقل البشري في خلقة أصل النوع البشري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r7.claim: The tree is presented as visible, but reports identifying its species are weak; he refers that discussion to al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r7.anchor: والإشارة إلى شجرة مشاهدة وقد رويت روايات ضعيفة في تعيين نوعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r8.claim: The Qur’an distributes Adam’s favors among accounts to renew listeners’ interest, vary the narration, and serve its main goals of moral instruction and example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p54#2/r8.anchor: ليحصل تجديد الفائدة ، تنشيطا للسامع ، وتفننا في أساليب الحكاية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r1.claim: The subjunctive after the prohibition presents becoming wrongdoers as a consequence of approaching the forbidden tree, not as a consequence of the act of prohibition itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r1.anchor: وانتصب : { فتكونا } على جواب النهي ، والكون من الظالمين متسبب على القرب المنهي عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r2.claim: Subjunctive response tracks causation from the forbidden action; a jussive response instead treats the result as an answer to the prohibition’s speech act, by analogy with a condition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r2.anchor: أن يعتبر التسبب على الفعل المنفي أو المنهي ، بخلاف الجزم في جواب النهي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r3.claim: The ‘wrongdoers’ are those who deserve that description either by harming themselves through bad consequences or by violating God’s right to obedience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p55#2/r3.anchor: إما لظلمهم أنفسهم وإلقائها في العواقب السيئة ، وإما لاعتدائهم على حق غيرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r8.claim: When several formulations suit the context, the eloquent speaker may choose either or use both for variety; Quranic variation refreshes repeated material with a changed nuance and style.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r8.anchor: إن المقام قد يقتضي شيئين متساويين أو أشياء متساوية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r9.claim: Adam’s eating is linked by و in 2:35 but by ف in 7:19; the village command varies between enter and dwell, with coordination and consequence both fitting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p117/r9.anchor: وقوله في الأعراف ) فكلا ( بفاء التفريع وكلاهما مطابق للمقام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r1.claim: A command to do what someone already does tells them to continue and persist in that state.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r1.anchor: إذا أمر الإنسان بشيء هو متلبس به فإنما المقصد بذلك أن يستمر على حاله ويتمادى في هيئته.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r2.claim: أنت emphasizes the hidden subject of اسكن and permits coordination with زوجك; the hidden pronoun especially needs emphasis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r2.anchor: وأكد الضمير الذي في قوله اسكن بقوله أنت وحينئذ جاز العطف عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r3.claim: فكلا derives from أكل; its initial radical is omitted in this imperative pattern, partly to avoid a difficult vowel on a weak letter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r3.anchor: وقوله: فكلا هو من أكل فأصله أكلا فحذفت فاء الفعل لاجتماع المثلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r4.claim: The verb is also used as قرب يقرب.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r4.anchor: ويقال قرب يقرب، وهذه الشجرة الظاهر أنه أشار إلى شخص شجرة واحدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r5.claim: The demonstrative may indicate one tree of a kind, or one individual while meaning the whole kind, as in generic singulars.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r5.anchor: ويحتمل أن يشير إلى شجرة معينة وهو يريد النوع بجملته، وعبر باسم الواحدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r6.claim: Most exegetes say Adam knowingly intended the forbidden act; Iblis claimed the ban was meant to prevent immortality or angelhood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وعلى الاحتمالين فآدم عليه السلام إنما قصد في وقت معصية فعل ما نهي عنه قاله جمهور المتأولين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects the claim that Adam mistook the ban as applying to one tree and ate another: this cannot explain why Iblis's promise persuaded him to violate what he thought allowed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382/r7.anchor: فيبطل بهذا قول من قال إن آدم إنما أخطأ متأولا بأن ظن النهي متعلقا بشخص شجرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r1.claim: The final ha in هذه is a ya changed at pause and retained in connected speech; Ibn Muhaysin's هذي preserves the original form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r1.anchor: والهاء الأخيرة في هذه بدل من الياء في هذي أبدلت في الوقف ثم ثبتت في الوصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r2.speaker: ابن محيصن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r2.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads هذي الشجرة, preserving the original form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن «هذي الشجرة» على الأصل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r3.claim: فتكونا is subjunctive as the response to the prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: فتكونا نصب في جواب النهي.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r4.claim: Jurists discuss how to judge unprecedented cases without a specific Qur'anic, Prophetic, or consensus ruling, then consider analogy and the default status of acts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r4.anchor: وتعلق الناس بهذه الآية في مسألة الحظر والإباحة، وذلك أن مسألة الحظر والإباحة تكلم الناس فيها على ضربين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r5.claim: One juristic view defaults to prohibition and caution: omission of a new case does not authorize people to legislate its permissibility.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r5.anchor: فقال بعضهم إذا نزل مثل هذا فنحمله على الحظر ونأخذ فيه بالشدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r6.claim: Another juristic view defaults to permissibility until a prohibition appears, since God completed the religion and would not leave people ignorant of an intended ban.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم بل نحملها على الإباحة لأن الله عز وجل قد أكمل لنا ديننا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r7.claim: A third juristic view suspends judgment and continues inquiry because cases require a specific or general revealed ruling; Ibn Atiyya calls this clearest.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم بل نحمل ذلك على الوقف أبدا ولا نحكم فيه بحظر ولا إباحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r8.claim: The jurists' debate concerns deriving rulings from revelation, not whether reason independently makes actions good or bad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r8.anchor: وهذا أبين الأقوال ولم يتعرض الفقهاء في هذه المسألة إلى النظر في تحسين العقل وتقبيحه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r9.speaker: المعتزلة ومن قال بقولهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r9.claim: The Muʿtazila frame the issue through rational good and evil, imagining a time or person without revelation, or Adam before earthly commands.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r9.anchor: وأما الضرب الثاني من كلام الناس في الحظر والإباحة فإن المعتزلة ومن قال بقولهم إن العقل يحسن ويقبح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r10.claim: One rationalist view holds everything prohibited until permission arrives, since using another's property is an encroachment, especially in relation to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r10.anchor: فقال بعضهم الذي يحسن في العقل أن تكون محظورة كلها حتى يرد الإذن باستباحتها، وذلك أن استباحتها تعد على ملك الغير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r11.speaker: بعض هذه الفرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r11.claim: Some in that group exempt breathing and movement because they cannot do otherwise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p382#2/r11.anchor: وذهب بعض هذه الفرقة إلى استثناء التنفس والحركة من هذا الحظر وقالوا إن هذه لا يمكن غيرها.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says necessity could make breathing and movement permissible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: ويمكن أن يقدر الاضطرار إليها إباحة لها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r2.claim: Another rationalist view allows harmless use of another's property, such as shade by a wall, and argues this is all the more permissible with God, who suffers no harm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: بل يحسن في العقل أن تكون مباحة إذ التحكم في ملك الغير بوجه لا ضرر عليه فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r3.speaker: أهل الحق والسنة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r3.claim: The people of truth and Sunna say reason alone establishes neither binding good nor bad; such judgments arise only through revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r3.anchor: وقال أهل الحق والسنة في هذا النحو من النظر، بل الأمر في نفسه على الوقف ولا يوجب العقل تحسينا ولا تقبيحا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r4.claim: Some say reason is never without revelation, making the hypothetical meaningless; Adam received commands in Paradise, including praise after sneezing and instructions to dwell, eat, and avoid the tree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: والعقل لم يخل قط من شرع، فلا معنى للخوض في هذه المسألة ولا لفرض ما لا يقع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r5.speaker: القاضي ابن الباقلاني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r5.claim: In al-Taqrib wa-l-Irshad, Ibn al-Baqillani says jurists adopted the Muʿtazili argument without realizing its implications.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r5.anchor: وقال القاضي ابن الباقلاني في التقريب والإرشاد: إن الفقهاء الذين قالوا بالحظر والإباحة لم يقصدوا الكون مع المعتزلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya objects that this disparages jurists: they derived rulings for new cases from revelation and should not be accused of rejecting this theological principle.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r6.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام حمل على فقهاء الشرع واستقصار لهم، والصواب أن لا يظن بهم هذا الخلل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya points back to his earlier discussion in al-Baqara about which tree it was.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p383/r7.anchor: وقد تقدم في سورة البقرة ذكر الاختلاف في الشجرة وتعيينها.

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r4.claim: Adam’s wife is Eve; the masculine wording is used because the possessive relation to Adam conveys the intended meaning concisely.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r4.anchor: وياآدم اسكن أنت وزوجك يعني حواء وذكرها بلفظ التذكير؛

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r5.speaker: أبو علي وأبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r5.claim: One view identifies this garden as a garden among the gardens of heaven.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r5.anchor: قيل: جنة من جنان السماء، عن أبي علي وأبي هاشم.

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r6.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r6.claim: A group identifies the garden as the Garden of Eternity; this is the choice of Ali ibn Isa.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r6.anchor: وقيل: جنة الخلد عن جماعة، وهو اختيار علي بن عيسى،

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r7.claim: The story is repeated because the Quran descended over twenty-odd years amid changing circumstances and visiting delegations, so new listeners could hear it as instruction and kindness.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r7.anchor: والفائدة في إعادتها أن القرآن نزل في بضع وعشرين سنة، والعوارض تعرض، والوفود تقدم،

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r8.claim: Repeating one story in different, excellent formulations is one aspect of the Quran’s inimitability.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r8.anchor: ولأن في إعادة قصة واحدة في مواضع بألفاظ مختلفة كل واحد في نهاية الحسن من إعجاز القرآن

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r9.claim: The command to eat grants permission to enjoy the garden’s blessings wherever they wish.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r9.anchor: فكلا هو إباحة بأمر من حيث شئتما أي: من نعيمها

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r10.claim: Not approaching the tree means avoiding it.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r10.anchor: ولا تقربا أي: تجنبا هذه الشجرة

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r11.speaker: الأكثر
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r11.claim: Most hold that the prohibition was binding and legally prohibitive; another view treats it as a nonbinding discouragement.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r11.anchor: وقيل: هو نهي وتحريم إلزام، وقيل: نهي تنزيه، والأكثر على الأول،

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r12.claim: One reported identification of the forbidden tree is the grapevine.

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r13.claim: Another reported identification of the forbidden tree is wheat.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r13.anchor: قيل: البر، والشجرة اسم لكل ما له ساق،

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r14.claim: The word tree can denote anything with a trunk.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r14.anchor: والشجرة اسم لكل ما له ساق، فتكونا من الظالمين

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r15.claim: They would wrong themselves by eating from it; the wording is a threat.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r15.anchor: فتكونا من الظالمين لأنفسكما بأكلها، وهذا وعيد.

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r16.claim: One explanation of their lapse is that they forgot the threat and thought the prohibition was only discouraging.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r16.anchor: قيل: نسيا الوعيد، وظنا أنه نهي تنزيه.

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r17.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r17.claim: Abu Ali explains that they misread the prohibition as applying to one particular tree, then ate from the same kind; the author calls this the soundest view.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r17.anchor: وقيل: أخطآ في التأويل، وظنا أن النهي عن شجرة بعينها لا عن جنسها، فأكلا من الجنس، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v4p2520/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r18.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r18.claim: A third explanation is that they forgot the prohibition; the author says a prohibition is not binding when forgotten, supporting Abu Ali’s view.
JISHUMI:v4p2520/r18.anchor: وقيل: نسيا النهي، والأصح ما قاله أبو علي؛ لأنه عند النسيان النهي لا يؤخذ به.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p90#3/r1.claim: The address يا آدم is explained as God saying to Adam, ‘O Adam.’

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r1.anchor: يعني حواء , وفي الجنة التي أمر بسكناها قولان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r2.claim: The garden may be the promised Garden of Eternity, from which departure was possible because it was not a reward requiring permanent residence, or an earthly garden without duties, although Adam himself was obligated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r2.anchor: وفي الجنة التي أمر بسكناها قولان : أحدهما : في جنة الخلد التي وعد المتقون , وجاز الخروج منها لأنها لم تجعل ثوابا

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r3.claim: Permission may cover any place throughout the garden, or any of its fruits, since the forbidden tree was fruit-bearing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r3.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : من حيث شئتما من الجنة كلها . والثاني : ما شئتما من الثمار كلها لأن المستثنى بالنهي لما كان ثمرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the forbidden tree as wheat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r4.anchor: أحدها : أنه البر , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the forbidden tree as a grapevine.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r6.speaker: بان جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the forbidden tree as a fig tree.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r7.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib identifies it as a camphor tree.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r7.anchor: والرابع : شجرة الكافور , قاله علي بن أبي طالب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies it as the tree of knowledge.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r9.speaker: ابن جدعان
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jud'an identifies it as the tree of eternity, which the angels ate from.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r9.anchor: والسادس : أنها شجرة الخلد التي كانت تأكل منها الملائكة , قاله ابن جدعان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r10.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r10.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from the People of the Two Books that it was a colocynth tree, but al-Mawardi says he knows no basis for this report.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r10.anchor: وحكى محمد بن إسحاق عن أهل الكتابين أنها شجرة الحنظل ولا أعرف لهذا وجها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r11.claim: The prohibition despite their complete knowledge served to preserve that knowledge and test them in a matter for which they would receive recompense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p208#2/r11.anchor: فإذا قيل : فما وجه نهيهما عن ذلك مع كمال معرفتهما ؟ قيل : المصلحة في استدامة

MUQATIL:7:19-21/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r1.claim: Muqatil identifies the forbidden tree as a wheat stalk.
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r1.anchor: ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة } ، وهي السنبلة الحنطة

MUQATIL:7:19-21/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r2.claim: He also reports an unnamed view that it was the tree beneath which angels rub themselves to gain immortality.
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r2.anchor: وقالوا: هي الشجرة التى تحتك بها الملائكة للخلود

MUQATIL:7:19-21/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:19-21/r3.claim: Eating from the tree would make Adam and his wife wrong themselves.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r1.claim: God addressed Adam after expelling Iblīs from the Garden.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r1.anchor: وقلنا يا آدم بعد إخراج ابليس من الجنة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r2.claim: «Dwell» means take the Garden as your residence.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r3.claim: They could eat wherever they wished but were forbidden to approach the tree lest they become wrongdoers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p6#2/r3.anchor: فكلا من حيث شئتما ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة فتكونا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:19/r1.claim: After Iblis was expelled from his place in heaven, Adam and Eve were told to dwell in the Garden; al-Qurtubi refers to his discussion of dwelling and the tree in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:19/r1.anchor: قال لآدم بعد إخراج إبليس من موضعه من السماء: اسكن أنت وحواء الجنة. وقد تقدم في البقرة معنى الإسكان

BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r1.claim: The passage cites a report that God forgives believers' mountain-sized sins and places them on Jews and Christians.
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r1.anchor: بذنوب أمثال الجبال فيغفرها الله لهم ويضعها على اليهود والنصارى

BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r2.claim: He says it accords with divine favor toward believers to ransom them through unbelievers: justice toward sinners and grace toward the obedient, against Mu'tazila denial.
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r2.anchor: ولا يستبعد من فضل الله مع أهل الإسلام والإيمان أن يفديهم بأهل الكفر والطغيان

BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r3.claim: The Mu'tazila cite 6:164, but 29:13 says unbelievers bear their own and additional burdens; each unbeliever is still punished for their own sin.
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r3.anchor: فلا يصح استدلالهم بالآية لأن كل كافر معاقب بوزره والله أعلم بحقيقة الحال

BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r4.claim: God addressed Adam after expelling Iblis from the Garden.
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r4.anchor: {ويااادم} أي : وقلنا لآدم بعد إخراج إبليس من الجنة يا آدم

BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r5.claim: The command means reside in a way that permits their stay and honors them.
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r5.anchor: أي : لازم الإقامة على طريق الإباحة والتكريم

BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r6.anchor: حواء والزوج في كلام العرب هو العدد

BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r7.claim: In Arabic زوج can mean the single counterpart in a pair; two companions are called زوجان.
BURSEVI:v3p109#2/r7.anchor: والزوج في كلام العرب هو العدد الفرد المزاوج لصاحبه فأما الاثنان المصطحبان

BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r1.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r1.claim: Most scholars hold this is the Garden of eternal recompense.
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r1.anchor: جنة الخلد التي جعلت دار الجزاء وعليه أكثر أهل العلم لوجوه ذكروها في كتبهم

BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r2.speaker: بعض المحققين من أهل الظاهر والباطن
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r2.claim: Some careful outward and inward scholars say it was either a garden in heaven from which they descended or an earthly garden elevated above the surrounding land.
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r2.anchor: أو جنة في السماء هبطا منها أو جنة في الأرض كانت مرتفعة على سائر بقاع الأرض

BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين من أهل الظاهر والباطن
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r3.claim: They argue it was a test garden: the final Garden has no prohibition; Adam slept, was expelled, and Iblis entered, unlike the Garden of recompense.
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r3.anchor: لأنه كلف فيها أن لا يأكل من تلك الشجرة ولا تكليف في الجنة الجزائية

BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r4.claim: A report says Adam craved grapes from the Garden at death; his sons went to find them, but angels met them and tended to Adam's burial.
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r4.anchor: ولما روي أن آدم لما احتضر اشتهى قطفا من عنب الجنة فانطلق بنوه ليطلبوه فلقيتهم الملائكة

BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r5.claim: He concludes Adam's garden was on earth: his sons sought its grapes, and the Nile is said to emerge from the Garden, which he identifies with earthly gardens.
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r5.anchor: وقد ثبت أن النيل يخرج من الجنة ولا شك أنها من جنان الأرض

BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r6.claim: The pair could eat wherever they wished and freely enjoy the Garden's fruits and blessings.
BURSEVI:v3p109#3/r6.anchor: من أي مكان شئتما ، ومن أي شيء شئتما

BURSEVI:v3p110/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110/r1.claim: God left the tree unidentified; if naming it benefited people, He would have specified it, as Akam al-Marjan says.
BURSEVI:v3p110/r1.anchor: اختلفوا في هذه الشجرة أيضا وقد أبهم الله ذكرها وتعيينها

BURSEVI:v3p110/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p110/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p110/r2.anchor: أي : فتصيرا من الذين ظلموا أنفسهم

RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r1.claim: Razi lists ten issues deferred to al-Baqara: whether dwelling is worship or permission, Eve’s creation, the garden’s location, eating as permission, prohibition as disapproval or ban, tree identity and kind, sin severity, injustice and condemnation, and whether this preceded Adam’s prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r1.anchor: فهذه المسائل العشرة قد سبق تفصيلها وتقريرها في سورة البقرة

RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r2.claim: The remaining difference from 2:35 is waw there versus fa here: waw gives conjunction generally, while fa adds succession, so succession is a subtype of conjunction.

RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r3.claim: Razi resolves the wording difference by saying al-Baqara gives the general category, while al-Aʿraf specifies the particular kind of conjunction.
RAZI-FULL:v14p37#3/r3.anchor: ففي سورة البقرة ذكر الجنس وفي سورة الأعراف ذكر النوع

BURHAN:v4p107/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p107/r3.speaker: ابن عمرون وابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p107/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUmarūn and Ibn Mālik require coordinated nouns to be capable of the same syntactic role; they therefore analyze زوجك as a separate clause with an omitted command to dwell.
BURHAN:v4p107/r3.anchor: وشرط ابن عمرون صاحبه ابن مالك فيه إن يصح إن يسند أحدهما إلى ما أسند إلى الآخر

BURHAN:v4p107/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p107/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BURHAN:v4p107/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that restriction: feminine Hind and masculine Zayd can be coordinated in تقوم هند وزيد even though Zayd alone cannot be the feminine verb’s subject.
BURHAN:v4p107/r4.anchor: ورد عليه الشيخ أثير الدين أبو حيان بأنه لا خلاف في صحة تقوم هند وزيد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r4.claim: The Quran uses zauj for Adam's spouse, including in 2:35, 7:19, and 20:117.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p229/r4.anchor: البيان القرآني يستعمل لفظ "زوج" حيثما تحدث عن آدم وزوجه: (آيات البقرة 35 والأعراف 19 وطه 117)
